title: Sweep the bay
brief:
A challenge for anyone who has finished the other tasks. Bottles are scattered across the whole bay, four rows deep. The drone starts in the bottom-left corner facing east and must pick up every bottle. Where it finishes does not matter.

Plan before you type. A good approach is a zigzag: clean one row from left to right, move up one row, clean the next row from right to left, and so on. Decompose the problem into helpers such as `clean_row()` and `go_up_and_turn()`, and think about the pre- and post-conditions of each one.

Nothing here is new - it is loops, if-statements and helper functions, combined. That is what programming is.

vocabulary.gloss: breaking a large problem into smaller, more manageable sub-problems - in code, into several short functions.
a loop that keeps repeating as long as a condition is true: `while front_is_clear():`
a decision with two paths: one block runs if the condition is true, the `else` block runs if it is false.
what must be true before a function is called, for example “the robot is facing east”.
what is true after the function has finished, for example “the robot is on the next corner, facing east”.

hints: Clean a row: `while front_is_clear(): clean_square(); move()` and then `clean_square()` once more.

At the end of a row, the drone needs to turn towards the next row (left if it was going east, right if it was going west), move one square, and turn again. Use `facing_east()` to decide which way to turn.
